payload.description:
Run a cheap detection census on materialized corpus packets so we know how much of today's 0% component recall is genuine non-detection versus vocabulary mismatch.

Recorded context (do not re-derive):

- `subType` is populated on 100% of emitted components in the measured packets (5/5 typescript-basic, 3/3 easy-school).
- `type:name` emits `asset:django orm` where gold says `asset:database` (subtype already holds `database`). For third parties the fields invert.
- `flask-login` emits **zero** components against gold claiming two positives. Some of the 0% is genuine non-detection, not vocabulary.
- Under one-to-one matching, an identity-only fix does **not** take easy-school from 1/3 to 2/3 — the engine emitted one database and gold carries two `asset:database` annotations. What the identity fix is worth depends on the KDATAP-471fdc cardinality ruling.

This census answers: on real repositories, how many components/flows/mentions/data items does the engine actually emit, and how many gold positives have no corresponding finding of any identity?

Blocked on `benchmark:materialize` working. AI inference stays disabled. No detector retuning, no new language ingest.

If the engine finds little on real repositories, **escalate**. Component recall would then be a detector problem wearing a vocabulary costume, and the sequencing of ~750 hand adjudications deserves review before that spend.

Definition of done: per-packet emission counts vs accepted gold counts, with a note on packets that emit nothing in a layer gold claims. No baseline is published from this run.
payload.title: Detection census: how much of 0% is genuine non-detection
